title: Vatican confirms Pope Leo underwent surgery for lung cancer
summary: The pope has had part of his lung removed and is recovering after surgery. Leo has been unusually candid for a pontiff about his health issues, disclosing the surgery to thousands of people in St.…

image.caption: Leo was greeted by the hospital's medical director, Andrea Cambieri, before he went in for his procedureImage: Guglielmo Mangiapane/REUTERS

blocks.text: Pope Leo XIV underwent surgery on Tuesday to remove a nodule from his lung that later was reported to be cancerous, the Vatican said, adding the pope "woke up normally" after the procedure.
"The procedure was completed successfully, within the expected timeframe and as planned," said a brief Vatican statement.
The Vatican ​said in a medical bulletin that he lower lobe of Leo's right lung was removed, and he was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, a common ​form of lung cancer.
The Vatican said the diagnosis had been suspected by preoperative tests and was confirmed during surgery.

The surgery at Rome's prestigious Gemelli hospital, which has been the main site of treatment for popes for decades, lasted about 7 hours. Leo's recovery is expected to ​take about a week, the statement added.
According to oncologists, Leo has an excellent prognosis since the cancerous nodule was caught so early.
A Vatican source cited by AFP news agency said further tests were being carried out to determine if the cancer had spread further.
Leo, 71, disclosed the health issue to thousands of worshippers at a prayer service on Sunday, making a marked shift in the level of transparency about his health compared to his predecessors.
In the past, the Vatican has often been accused of making confusing or extremely vague statements about popes' health, if revealing at information at all.
All of the pontiff's engagements have been cancelled through October 20. He is still likely to take a planned trip to South America in November.
